name: Agriculture & Agribusiness
one_liner: Producing, processing and trading crops and livestock, a weather- and commodity-exposed system whose value pools sit mostly with inputs and traders rather than farmers.
how_it_makes_money: Farmers sell crops and livestock at commodity prices, supplemented by crop insurance and government programs. Input suppliers sell seeds, crop protection, fertilizer and equipment, often at attractive margins due to IP and brand. Traders and processors earn thin spreads on buying, storing, moving and converting commodities into food, feed and fuel.
revenue_formula: Farm revenue = acres planted × yield per acre × price per bushel
Input revenue = acres treated × application rate × price per unit
Trader margin = volume handled × spread per tonne
cost_structure: Land: rent or ownership, a major fixed cost for farmers
Seed, fertilizer and crop protection inputs
Labor, especially in specialty crops and livestock
Feed: the largest cost in livestock production
margins: Farm-level margins are thin and volatile with weather and prices, while seed, crop protection and equipment makers earn higher, steadier margins. Traders and processors run on thin margins but large volumes. IP, scale, and exposure to commodity cycles drive the spread.

key_metrics.name: Yield per acre
key_metrics.what: Output per unit of land, the core farm productivity measure.

key_metrics.name: Crop prices (corn, soybeans, wheat)
key_metrics.what: Drive farm income and input spending.

key_metrics.name: Farm income
key_metrics.what: Aggregate farmer profitability, which drives equipment and input demand.

key_metrics.name: Crush / processing margin
key_metrics.what: Spread between raw crop and processed products like meal and oil.

key_metrics.name: Input cost per acre
key_metrics.what: Total spending per acre, used to assess farmer breakeven.

key_metrics.name: Stocks-to-use ratio
key_metrics.what: Inventory relative to consumption, a key price signal.

trends: Precision agriculture, autonomy and data-driven farming
Trade tensions and tariffs disrupting export markets like soybeans
Renewable diesel and biofuels boosting demand for vegetable oils
Climate volatility increasing yield and price risk
Consolidation in seeds, crop protection and farm operations
Regenerative agriculture and sustainability demands from food companies
